title: Taxonomic search and reporting for human-depleted CSF metagenomic reads

sources.revision: retrieved 2026-09-30; wiki revision not pinned by repository commit
sources.locator: Metagenomic pathogen detection; The Dataset; Assigning taxonomic labels; Visualizing taxonomic results; Investigating the pathogen
query database creation, taxonomy invocation and result/report handling

scientific_use: Search a human-depleted patient CSF metagenomic read set against taxonomically annotated Swiss-Prot proteins, summarize lowest-common-ancestor assignments, and filter reads assigned to a candidate taxon for follow-up. The tutorial frames this as investigating an encephalitis pathogen; its questions require biological interpretation beyond the command output.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial composes existing MMseqs2 commands (createdb, createtaxdb, taxonomy, createtsv, taxonomyreport, filtertaxdb, createsubdb, convert2fasta); no underlying method implementation is performed.

inputs.meaning: Tutorial-provided FASTA of CSF sequencing reads after human-read removal; article/tutor text says the original run returned 14 million short nucleotide reads and the released reduced set has 226,908 reads. Tutorial says paired reads may have been merged with FLASH. Exact SRA run/accession for this patient's sequence file was not identified in inspected sources.
inputs.stage: human-depleted and tutorial-prepared read set; query to protein-reference taxonomy search
inputs.metadata: patient CSF, hospital day 8, metagenomic sequencing; human-read removal with Kraken; exact sample/run accession, read pairing/merge status for supplied FASTA unresolved

inputs.meaning: Swiss-Prot protein sequences plus accession-to-taxonomy mapping, converted into MMseqs2 sequence and taxonomy databases before search
inputs.format: FASTA.GZ plus TSV.GZ mapping, then MMseqs2 seqTaxDb
inputs.stage: reference protein database with taxonomy annotations
inputs.metadata: tutorial uses uniprot_sprot_2018_03.fasta.gz and uniprot_sprot_2018_03_mapping.tsv.gz; its text describes about 500,000 proteins

outputs.meaning: Per-read LCA result database and tabular result with taxonomic identifiers/ranks/labels; summarized taxonomic abundance report or Krona HTML; optional taxon-filtered read-ID subset and reconstructed FASTA
outputs.format: MMseqs2 databases, TSV, text report or HTML, FASTA
outputs.stage: search-derived assignments and downstream report/filter products
outputs.metadata: Tutorial asks users to interpret common taxa and distinguish possible environmental/reagent/background sequences from actual CSF presence; no result values independently verified.

dependencies: MMseqs2 commands createdb, createtaxdb, taxonomy, createtsv, taxonomyreport, filtertaxdb, createsubdb, convert2fasta
MMseqs2 taxonomy database requires mapping/taxonomy setup; tutorial provides archived 2018-03 reference assets
SRA or tutorial file retrieval is external; no runtime or execution validation performed
evidence: Wiki patient/dataset and assignment sections describe CSF, day 8, original 14M reads, human-read removal, 226,908 released reads, reference setup and command sequence.
Wiki output/report sections specify read-level taxonomic labels and reports; README taxonomy summary says taxonomy workflow searches an annotated sequence database and computes LCA.
Repository easytaxonomy workflow creates query DB, runs taxonomy, and follows with output/report handling; source inspected at pinned commit.
Wiki's eukaryotic-read question cautions that taxonomy assignments alone do not establish that assigned organisms were present in the spinal-fluid sample.
limitations: Tutorial wiki content is mutable; retrieved 2026-09-30 and no wiki commit was pinned.
Exact sample run/accession and precise identity of downloadable mystery_reads.fasta relative to public SRA assets are unresolved; do not infer accession.
Result accuracy, contamination interpretation, suitability as a clinical diagnostic, and reproducibility are not tested.
Reuse terms for tutorial FASTA and 2018 Swiss-Prot snapshot were not inspected.

title: Six-frame contig taxonomic assignment by fragment voting

sources.revision: retrieved 2026-09-30; wiki revision not pinned by repository commit
sources.locator: Contig taxonomic assignment and auxiliary modules; Download SwissProt and its associated taxonomic information; Run the MMseqs2 taxonomy; Produce a TSV report; Produce a Krona/Kraken visualization
UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot selection and taxonomy setup branches

scientific_use: Assign taxonomy to a Saccharomyces cerevisiae genomic contig by extracting six-frame protein fragments, searching a taxonomically annotated Swiss-Prot database, and voting among fragment labels. The documented example reports a species label and evidence summary, then offers fragment and contig taxonomic reports.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial applies MMseqs2's existing taxonomy workflow and report commands to an input contig; it does not implement or alter the assignment method.

inputs.meaning: A segment file named NC_001133.9_100425_153163.fa retrieved from the metaeuk-regression repository; tutorial shows its header/accession and uses it as a contig. A separate 19-protein segment file is offered for viewing and explicitly is not used in this tutorial.
inputs.stage: single raw/reference contig input to createdb then taxonomy
inputs.metadata: accession NC_001133.9; example assignment says Saccharomyces cerevisiae, taxid 4932. Segment coordinate convention beyond filename not explained.

inputs.meaning: MMseqs2-downloadable Swiss-Prot sequences with associated taxonomy
inputs.format: sequence DB plus MMseqs2 seqTaxDb/taxonomy files
inputs.stage: protein reference database used for six-frame fragment search
inputs.metadata: The tutorial uses `mmseqs databases UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot`; snapshot/release unspecified and mutable.

outputs.meaning: Contig-level taxonomy record with lineage and counts/support fields, a TSV rendering, and optional fragment Krona or contig Kraken-format report
outputs.format: MMseqs2 taxonomy result DB, TSV, HTML/text report
outputs.metadata: Example reports taxid 4932, species Saccharomyces cerevisiae; 32 fragments passed prefilter, all 32 labeled, 30 agreeing with assigned taxon/descendant, reported -log(E-value) support fraction 0.890.

dependencies: MMseqs2 databases workflow and taxonomy/TaxPerContig workflow; MMseqs2 taxonomy, createtsv, taxonomyreport
Tutorial parameters: --tax-lineage 2, --majority 0.5, --vote-mode 1, --lca-mode 3, --orf-filter 1
Reference-database release changes because tutorial selects current Swiss-Prot
evidence: Wiki links contig FASTA to metaeuk-regression commit 205bc3f26bfa335366e2f00dccbc6900306cd4a8 and distinguishes optional unused 19-protein FASTA.
Wiki explains six-frame fragments, accelerated 2bLCA, weighted voting, and output lineage semantics and gives the exact example result.
Pinned repository databases.sh contains a Swiss-Prot selection branch; tutorial shell source access is pinned to repository revision.
limitations: Tutorial wiki revision and live Swiss-Prot release are not pinned; release gap affects reproducibility.
No sequence asset was downloaded or previewed and no MMseqs2 execution was performed.
Reported example result is tutorial-reported, not reproduced; taxonomy depends on the chosen reference and parameters.
Reuse terms for contig and Swiss-Prot assets were not established.

title: Cluster pathogen read assemblies into representative proteins

sources.revision: retrieved 2026-09-30; wiki revision not pinned by repository commit
sources.locator: Metagenomic pathogen detection; Investigating the pathogen; Assembling reads to proteins; Clustering to find representative proteins; Annotating the proteins
FASTA input creation, cluster output TSV, representative and member FASTA conversion

scientific_use: After filtering reads assigned to a candidate pathogen, assemble overlapping reads into protein sequences with Plass, use MMseqs2 easy-cluster to reduce similarity redundancy, and inspect representative sequences for expected pathogen proteins/domains. This follow-up is downstream of the taxonomy investigation and relies on its filtered reads.
tool_role_basis: It applies existing Plass and MMseqs2 software; no assembly or clustering algorithm is implemented in the tutorial.

inputs.meaning: FASTA of reads selected from the human-depleted CSF reads based on taxonomic assignments in the related unit
inputs.metadata: Selection is by user-supplied NCBI taxon ID(s); identity depends on preceding taxonomic inference

outputs.meaning: Plass protein assembly FASTA, MMseqs2 cluster membership TSV, all member sequences FASTA, and one representative sequence per cluster FASTA; representatives are suggested for external domain annotation
outputs.stage: assembled proteins then redundancy-reduced representative proteins
outputs.metadata: Tutorial asks for assembly/representative counts and comparison with expected proteins; no example counts provided here.

dependencies: Prior unit mmseqs2-wiki-pathogen-taxonomy and its pathogen_read_ids/reads_pathogen.fasta output
Plass assemble; MMseqs2 easy-cluster, which internally creates a sequence DB, clusters, and formats outputs
Optional MMseqs2 webserver annotation against PFAM, PDB and Uniclust
evidence: Tutorial specifies filtertaxdb to taxon-filtered IDs and createsubdb/convert2fasta reconstruction before Plass assembly.
Tutorial describes Plass assembly to find overlapping reads and easy-cluster outputs, including representative sequences.
Pinned easycluster.sh converts input sequences to a database, runs the configured clustering module, produces TSV, representative FASTA and all-sequence FASTA.
limitations: Scientific result depends on earlier candidate-taxonomy decision; a taxonomic hit is not independently confirmed pathogen presence.
The tutorial's webserver step is externally hosted and its target databases are mutable; current behavior was not checked.
No assemblies or searches were run; sequence counts and expected proteins remain unobserved.
Tutorial FASTA access/reuse terms remain unresolved.

title: Assemble a human-gut metagenome protein catalogue directly from paired reads

sources.revision: retrieved 2026-09-30; wiki revision not pinned by repository commit
sources.locator: Writing large scale sequence analysis workflows; Analysis of a human gut metagenomics dataset; Getting a protein catalogue of a metagenome

scientific_use: Generate a protein sequence catalogue from paired human-gut metagenomic reads using Plass protein-level assembly without a nucleotide assembly step, with a conventional MEGAHIT plus Prodigal metagenomic gene-calling route as a comparison. The tutorial proposes comparing the counts of protein sequences in the two FASTA outputs.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial applies existing Plass, MEGAHIT, and Prodigal software and compares their outputs; it does not implement these tools.

inputs.meaning: Paired-end FASTQ files for SRA run ERR1384114, obtainable using SRA Toolkit or the tutorial's paired ENA FASTQ URLs
inputs.metadata: Tutorial identifies sample as human gut metagenomic dataset; sample-level experimental design, collection, assay platform, and read counts not inspected.

outputs.meaning: Plass assembled protein catalogue FASTA; comparison outputs are MEGAHIT contigs and Prodigal-called protein FASTA; count of FASTA records is proposed as a simple output summary
outputs.stage: direct protein-level assembly and comparator nucleotide assembly/gene calling
outputs.metadata: Tutorial states standard genomic assembly may miss reads due to low coverage and micro-diversity and cites Plass recovery advantage as general paper claim; no outputs were generated here.

dependencies: SRA Toolkit (`prefetch`, `fasterq-dump`) or ENA paired FASTQ URLs
Plass; comparison route uses MEGAHIT and Prodigal with `-p meta`
Tutorial prerequisite section recommends Conda environment with these tools
evidence: Tutorial names SRA run ERR1384114, supplies exact paired ENA file paths and Plass command.
Tutorial specifies the alternative MEGAHIT assembly and Prodigal metagenomic protein-calling commands and suggests counting FASTA headers.
Tutorial motivates direct protein assembly in the context of low coverage and micro-diversity; execution and comparative findings for this run are not shown.
limitations: Repository is MMseqs2; central assembler/comparator are separate packages Plass, MEGAHIT, and Prodigal.
SRA metadata, exact sample count, assay/library details, and reuse terms were not checked.
No data downloaded or tools run; output and comparative claims for this run are not validated.

title: Reduce protein-catalogue redundancy with identity and coverage criteria

sources.locator: Writing large scale sequence analysis workflows; Redundancy reduction; Learn how to deal with MMseqs2's indexed databases
easycluster FASTA/database workflow and cluster output conversion

scientific_use: Cluster a Plass-derived metagenomic protein catalogue to reduce redundant sequences, using an example minimum identity 0.9, coverage 0.95 and target/member coverage mode; inspect representative sequences or cluster membership. The tutorial also shows the equivalent database-level `cluster` path and describes the cluster database representation.
tool_role_basis: MMseqs2 easy-cluster/cluster apply existing clustering operations to supplied sequences; the tutorial does not implement a clustering method.

inputs.meaning: Protein catalogue FASTA generated from the ERR1384114 paired reads by the prior protein-assembly unit
inputs.format: FASTA or corresponding MMseqs2 sequence database
inputs.stage: assembled protein sequences, before redundancy reduction
inputs.metadata: Demonstration command sets --min-seq-id 0.9 -c 0.95 --cov-mode 1; example catalogue output is not included in source repository.

outputs.meaning: Cluster assignment/member database and, for easy-cluster, cluster TSV, all-member FASTA, and representative-sequence FASTA; cluster database entry keys identify representative sequences and values list member keys
outputs.format: MMseqs2 cluster DB plus TSV and FASTA
outputs.metadata: Tutorial defines edge criteria through E-value, coverage mode, and minimum identity; default identity is an estimated correlated measure unless alignment mode requests direct identity.

dependencies: Upstream Plass protein catalogue from unit mmseqs2-wiki-gut-protein-assembly
MMseqs2 easy-cluster or cluster and createdb/createtsv/result2repseq/result2flat workflow components
Temporary directory and MMseqs2 indexed database conventions for native cluster route
evidence: Tutorial links catalogue redundancy to Plass assembly and gives easy-cluster command and representative FASTA filename.
Tutorial defines coverage modes and the default estimated identity semantics; notes cluster parameters are alignment-based criteria.
Tutorial explains createdb's indexed database and cluster DB key/value representation; pinned easycluster.sh confirms command workflow output formats.
limitations: Plass-produced input FASTA is a derived asset from ERR1384114; this inventory groups it with the source reads as a distinct processing stage, not as independent observations.
No clustering was executed and no cluster count, representative quality, runtime or suitability was assessed.
Identity behavior depends on MMseqs2 alignment mode and selected parameters; tutorial command does not explicitly set alignment mode.

inputs.format: Stockholm gzip, MMseqs2 MSA DB and profile DB

inputs.meaning: Representative protein sequences selected by cluster membership from Plass-derived catalogue
inputs.stage: representative subset from clustered metagenome protein catalogue
inputs.metadata: Tutorial uses cluster DB index to select representative keys from original catalogue DB.

outputs.format: MMseqs2 result DB, TSV, sequence DB and FASTA
outputs.stage: profile-search domain annotations and confidence-filtered subset

title: Map metagenomic ORFs to a protein catalogue and estimate protein abundance

sources.revision: retrieved 2026-09-30; wiki revision not pinned by repository commit
sources.locator: Writing large scale sequence analysis workflows; Abundance analysis

scientific_use: Estimate abundance of catalogue proteins by extracting ORFs from metagenomic reads, translating nucleotide ORFs, mapping translated reads to a protein catalogue, retaining significant full-coverage best hits, transposing results to group ORFs by target, and counting mapped ORFs. Tutorial also proposes aligned-length divided by protein length as an advanced abundance calculation.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial asks the user to compose existing MMseqs2 modules (createdb, extractorfs, translatenucs, prefilter, rescorediagonal, filterdb, swapresults, result2stats, createtsv, optionally apply); it does not implement a new algorithm.

inputs.meaning: Raw paired reads from the human-gut run and protein catalogue produced from those reads by upstream protein assembly
inputs.format: FASTQ/FASTA read inputs converted to MMseqs2 DB; amino-acid catalogue DB
inputs.stage: raw reads transformed to translated read ORFs, mapped against upstream assembled/catalogue proteins
inputs.metadata: Tutorial uses read database from paired files and `plassProteinsReduced` as catalogue name for the output TSV; exact construction and prior catalogue linkage is not completely repeated in this subsection.

outputs.meaning: Per-protein counts of mapped read-ORFs, optionally aligned-length/protein-length abundance estimates, formatted TSV
outputs.metadata: Tutorial specifies prefilter -s 2, rescorediagonal -c 1 --cov-mode 2 --min-seq-id 0.95 --rescore-mode 2 -e 0.000001 --sort-results 1, best target retention, result transposition, and result2stats count.

dependencies: MMseqs2 createdb, extractorfs, translatenucs, prefilter, rescorediagonal, filterdb, swapresults, result2stats, apply (advanced option), createtsv
Upstream protein catalogue produced from the same ERR1384114 reads; exact tutorial alias is `plassProteinsReduced`
No complete command script is provided: the tutorial gives an ordered module checklist and requested parameters.
evidence: Tutorial Abundance analysis explicitly frames objective as mapping ORFs from reads to protein catalogue and counting hits per protein.

Tutorial enumerates ORF extraction, translation, prefilter, gapless rescoring, best-target filtering, swapresults transposition, result2stats counting, optional length normalization, and TSV formatting.

Pinned translated_search.sh offers related translated sequence workflow implementation; the tutorial's proposed abundance pipeline is a distinct mapping/counting analysis and not identical to its standard translated search workflow.
limitations: The tutorial does not supply a full executable workflow and none was assembled or run here.
Abundance is operationally estimated from read-ORF hits; mapping ambiguity, normalization across protein lengths/coverage, and biological comparability are not otherwise resolved in this section.
Input protein catalogue is a derived stage of ERR1384114 data; source outputs are not included or previewed.
